content:
jonathan: quick question — we're evaluating using an app-managed identity in tenant A to unwrap keys in a Key Vault in tenant B. Anyone done cross-tenant Key Vault access with managed identities? Seems blocked by AAD boundary.

priya: short answer: you can't directly use a system-assigned MI from tenant A against a vault in tenant B. MI is tied to the subscription/tenant.

alex_r: options:
- create a service principal (app) in the vault's tenant and give it RBAC or access policy
- invite the app as a guest? (B2B) still messy for SPs
- run a proxy in the vault's tenant that accepts signed requests from tenant A

lia: also think about RBAC vs access policy here — are we using "Azure RBAC for Key Vault" or legacy access policies? RBAC is easier for assigning roles at subscription/resource group level, but some operations still need access policy? (keys/crypto operations should be covered by Key Vault Crypto Officer/DA roles)

mike_sre: from infra side: if you need cross-subscription without tenant hop, simplest is deploy a tiny token-exchange service in the vault tenant. If you control both tenants, create a service principal in the vault tenant and give it role assignment.

jonathan: got it. We're also doing envelope encryption: DEKs stored with metadata pointing to a KEK in Key Vault. How do people rotate KEKs without re-encrypting massive DEK sets?

priya: typical pattern:
1) create a new Key Vault key (new version or entirely new key)
2) for each DEK, do wrapKey with the new KEK (i.e., re-wrap the DEK) — this is cheap since DEKs are small
3) update the DEK metadata to point to the new key id/version
4) keep old KEK available to decrypt until all DEKs migrated, then schedule deletion/soft-delete

alex_r: note: if you use key versions under same key name you can rotate without changing key URI (but versioned URI changes). Our metadata stores the full key identifier (vault/key/version).

lia: audit logging and alerts — enable Key Vault diagnostic settings to send to Log Analytics/Storage/EventHub. Watch for operations like:
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/create
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/backup

keyvault-audit-bot: audit-event: 2025-10-05T14:22:10Z - key unwrap by servicePrincipalId=0x... resource=/subscriptions/..../vaults/rdw-kv keys/myk/versions/3

mike_sre: FYI: if vault has a private endpoint, remember to configure MSI/networking in the same VNet or use peered networks; cross-tenant private endpoints are a headache.

jonathan: what about RBAC vs access policies for crypto operations? I thought RBAC is now GA for keys.

lia: RBAC covers get/list/wrap/unwrap if you assign the appropriate Data Plane roles (Key Vault Crypto User/Officer). Access policies are legacy but sometimes easier for fine-grained per-key perms. Choose RBAC if you want unified IAM (recommended) and access policies if you need to migrate legacy permissions quickly.

priya: also check "Allow trusted Microsoft services" and tenant-level cross-tenant settings if you plan to accept tokens from another Azure AD. For partner scenarios, AAD cross-tenant access settings and entitlement management can help.

jonathan: thanks — last Q: any gotchas with rotation and purge-protection/soft-delete?

alex_r: enable soft-delete and purge-protection on prod vaults. When rotating, create new key/version, re-wrap DEKs, then schedule key deletion only after you confirm no clients point to old version. Purge-protection will prevent accidental permanent deletion.

mike_sre: if you need to do bulk rewrap, run a job that processes DEKs idempotently and report progress. Use Key Vault throttling backoffs and exponential retry — Key Vault has request limits.

jonathan: perfect. I'll draft a short runbook: (1) create new key, (2) set diag logs to LA, (3) run rewrap job with retries, (4) switchover metadata, (5) delete old key w/soft-delete, (6) purge only after 30d.

priya: lgtm :thumbsup:

lia: ping me when you have the runbook link, happy to review the audit/alerts part.

jonathan: will do — thanks everyone!
